chapter_title: Right Form of Verbs and Subject-Verb Agreement

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'The quality of the mangoes ______ genuinely exceptional.'
questions.explanation: The head noun subject is 'The quality' (singular uncountable), not the plural noun 'mangoes' inside the prepositional phrase. Hence the singular verb 'was' is required.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Slow and steady ______ the race.'
questions.explanation: When two singular nouns joined by 'and' express a single unified idea or compound concept ('slow and steady'), they take a singular verb ('wins').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Ten thousand dollars ______ a substantial sum of money for the research project.'
questions.explanation: Plural expressions of distance, money, periods of time, or measurement regarded as a single total take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Physics ______ always been her favorite academic discipline.'
questions.explanation: Nouns plural in form but singular in meaning (Physics, Mathematics, Economics, News) take singular verbs ('has').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'A large number of students ______ participating in the annual debate competition.'
questions.explanation: 'A number of + plural noun' takes a plural verb ('are'), whereas 'The number of + plural noun' takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'The teacher, along with his students, ______ attending the international conference.'
questions.explanation: When a subject is accompanied by phrases like 'along with', 'as well as', 'together with', or 'in addition to', the verb agrees with the primary first subject ('The teacher' = singular).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Rahim as well as his brothers ______ invited to the banquet.'
questions.explanation: With 'as well as', the verb agrees with the initial subject ('Rahim', singular), so 'was' is grammatically correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'The Prime Minister, accompanied by several cabinet ministers, ______ arrived at the summit.'
questions.explanation: The parenthetical phrase 'accompanied by...' does not affect subject-verb agreement; the verb agrees with 'The Prime Minister' (singular).

questions.question: 'Bread and butter ______ his only breakfast every morning.'
questions.explanation: 'Bread and butter' represents a single unified meal item, requiring the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Identify the correct verb: 'No passenger and no luggage ______ permitted on the runway.'
questions.explanation: When two singular subjects are preceded by 'no' or 'every', they take a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither the manager nor the employees ______ satisfied with the new policy.'
questions.explanation: In 'neither... nor...', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it ('the employees', plural), demanding 'were'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Either you or he ______ mistaken in this matter.'
questions.explanation: With 'either... or...', the verb agrees with the proximate subject ('he' = 3rd person singular), hence 'is'.

questions.question: 'Not only the captain but also the sailors ______ honored for their bravery.'
questions.explanation: In 'not only... but also...', the verb agrees with the second noun phrase ('the sailors', plural).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.label: A
options.text: Neither my brother nor I am interested in joining the corporate firm.

options.label: B
options.text: Neither my brother nor I are interested in joining the corporate firm.

options.label: C
options.text: Neither my brother nor I is interested in joining the corporate firm.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither my brother nor I were interested in joining the corporate firm.

questions.correct_answer_text: Neither my brother nor I am interested in joining the corporate firm.
questions.explanation: The closest subject to the verb is the first-person singular pronoun 'I', which correctly takes 'am'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Either the principal or the teachers ______ responsible for organizing the sports day.'
questions.explanation: 'Teachers' is plural and sits immediately adjacent to the verb, so 'are' is grammatically required.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'One of my closest friends ______ a senior software architect in Silicon Valley.'
questions.explanation: The structure 'One of + plural noun' always takes a singular verb ('is') because the subject is 'One'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Everyone in the auditorium ______ standing to applaud the national anthem.'
questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns ending in -one, -body, or -thing (everyone, somebody, anything) take singular verbs.

questions.question: When does a collective noun like 'jury' take a PLURAL verb?

options.label: A
options.text: When the members of the jury are divided in their individual opinions

options.label: B
options.text: Whenever the jury reaches a unanimous verdict

options.label: C
options.text: When the trial lasts more than one week

options.label: D
options.text: Collective nouns never take plural verbs

questions.correct_answer_text: When the members of the jury are divided in their individual opinions
questions.explanation: A collective noun (jury, committee) takes a plural verb when its members act as separate individuals with conflicting opinions ('The jury were divided in their opinions').

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Each of the participants ______ awarded a certificate of merit.'
questions.explanation: 'Each of + plural noun' is grammatically singular and takes the singular verb 'was'.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'The committee ______ submitted its unanimous annual report.'
questions.explanation: When a collective noun acts as a unified single body (indicated here by the pronoun 'its'), it takes a singular verb ('has').

questions.question: Choose the correct form of verb: 'He just (receive) ______ the letter from the university.'
questions.explanation: Time adverbs like 'just', 'already', 'recently', and 'yet' typically signal the present perfect tense ('has received').

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'I (see) ______ him walking across the park three days ago.'
questions.explanation: Past time markers like 'ago', 'yesterday', and 'last night' require the simple past tense ('saw').

questions.question: Complete the classic sequence: 'The patient (die) ______ before the doctor arrived.'
questions.explanation: In two past actions linked by 'before', the earlier action takes the past perfect ('had died') and the subsequent action takes the simple past ('arrived').

questions.question: 'The train started after I (reach) ______ the station.'
questions.explanation: When two past actions are joined by 'after', the clause following 'after' takes past perfect ('had reached').

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'By next December, we ______ in this house for ten years.'
questions.explanation: A duration extending up to a specified future point ('By next December... for ten years') takes the future perfect continuous tense.

questions.question: Complete the First Conditional: 'If it rains this afternoon, we ______ the match.'
questions.explanation: In first conditionals ('If + present simple'), the principal clause takes 'will + base verb' ('will postpone').

questions.question: Complete the Second Conditional: 'If I knew his contact number, I ______ him immediately.'
questions.explanation: In second conditionals representing unreal present situations ('If + past simple'), the result clause takes 'would + base verb' ('would call').

questions.question: Complete the Third Conditional: 'If they had invited him cordially, he ______ the celebration.'
questions.explanation: In third conditionals representing unreal past conditions ('If + past perfect'), the consequence clause requires 'would have + past participle'.

questions.question: 'Had I possessed wings like a dove, I ______ across the oceans.'
questions.explanation: An inverted third conditional beginning with 'Had I + past participle' is completed by 'would have + past participle' ('would have flown').

questions.question: Complete the Zero Conditional expressing scientific truth: 'If water is heated to 100 degrees Celsius, it ______.'
questions.explanation: Zero conditionals express scientific or universal laws; both clauses use the present simple tense ('heats... boils').

questions.question: Which verb is typically followed directly by a GERUND (verb+ing) rather than an infinitive?
questions.explanation: Verbs like 'avoid', 'enjoy', 'mind', 'deny', 'postpone', and 'admit' are followed by gerunds (e.g. 'avoid making mistakes').

questions.question: 'Would you mind ______ the window? It is quite chilly inside.'
questions.explanation: The polite request structure 'Would you mind...' is strictly followed by a gerund ('closing').

questions.question: What is the difference in verb form between 'used to' and 'is used to'?

options.label: A
options.text: 'Used to' takes a base verb (past habit), whereas 'is used to' takes a gerund (accustomed to something)

options.label: B
options.text: 'Used to' takes a past participle, 'is used to' takes an infinitive

options.label: D
options.text: 'Used to' is only used in negative sentences

questions.correct_answer_text: 'Used to' takes a base verb (past habit), whereas 'is used to' takes a gerund (accustomed to something)
questions.explanation: 'He used to swim' (past habit + base verb) vs 'He is used to swimming' (be accustomed to + gerund).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He went to the bookstore with a view to ______ reference dictionaries.'
questions.explanation: 'With a view to' ends in a preposition and must be followed by a gerund ('purchasing').

questions.question: Identify the participle in: 'The barking dog rarely bites.'

options.label: A
options.text: barking (Present Participle acting as an adjective)

questions.correct_answer_text: barking (Present Participle acting as an adjective)
questions.explanation: 'Barking' is a present participle (verb+ing) modifying the noun 'dog' as a descriptive verbal adjective.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: 'You had better ______ a doctor without further delay.'
questions.explanation: 'Had better' behaves as a modal idiom followed by a bare infinitive (base form of verb without 'to': 'consult').

questions.question: In causative constructions with 'make', which form of verb follows the agent?
questions.explanation: Active causative 'make' requires a bare infinitive: 'The teacher made the student apologize' (not 'to apologize').

questions.question: 'I had my automobile ______ by an expert mechanic yesterday.'
questions.explanation: In passive causative 'have/get something done', when an object receives the action, the past participle ('repaired') is used.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The mother let her child ______ outside in the garden.'
questions.explanation: Causative 'let' is followed by a bare infinitive ('let him play').

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He got his brother ______ the heavy carton to the attic.'
questions.explanation: Active causative 'get' requires a full infinitive with 'to' ('get someone to do something').

topics.topic_name: Special Constructions (As If, As Though, It is high time)

questions.question: Complete the sentence correctly: 'He talks as if he (know) ______ everything.'
questions.explanation: When the main clause is present tense ('He talks'), 'as if / as though' takes a past subjunctive ('knew' or 'were') to denote unreal pretense.

questions.question: 'He behaved as if he (be) ______ the owner of the mansion.'
questions.explanation: In hypothetical/unreal clauses after 'as if', the subjunctive 'were' is used for all persons and numbers.

questions.question: 'He spoke as though he (witness) ______ the incident with his own eyes.' (Main clause in past tense)
questions.explanation: When the main clause preceding 'as though' is in the past tense ('He spoke'), the subsequent clause takes the past perfect ('had witnessed').

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'It is high time we (change) ______ our corrupt habits.'
questions.explanation: The idiom 'It is high time / It is time' followed by a subject clause strictly requires the simple past tense ('changed') to express urgent necessity.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.label: A
options.text: I wish I were a philologist studying ancient scripts.

options.label: B
options.text: I wish I was a philologist studying ancient scripts.

options.label: C
options.text: I wish I am a philologist studying ancient scripts.

options.label: D
options.text: I wish I have been a philologist studying ancient scripts.

questions.correct_answer_text: I wish I were a philologist studying ancient scripts.
questions.explanation: In formal English, unreal subjunctive wishes about the present require 'were' instead of 'was'.

topics.topic_name: Passive Voice and Board Exam Passage Integration

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the right form of verb: 'English (speak) ______ all over the world as an international lingua franca.'
questions.explanation: English does not speak itself; it is spoken by people worldwide, requiring the present simple passive 'is spoken'.

questions.question: 'Paper (invent) ______ in ancient China centuries ago.'
questions.explanation: A past historical event with a passive subject takes the past simple passive ('was invented').

questions.question: 'The building is currently under construction; it (complete) ______ by next December.'
questions.explanation: Future passive with specified deadline requires 'will be + past participle' ('will be completed').

questions.question: Fill the blank in the board-style cloze text: 'Corruption must (uproot) ______ if the nation is to prosper.'
questions.explanation: Modal passive construction requires 'modal + be + past participle' ('must be uprooted').

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence: 'Walk fast lest you ______ miss the morning express train.'
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'lest' ('for fear that') is followed by a clause containing 'should' + base verb (or subjunctive base verb).
